title: AL-Go issue triage findings
description: The typed contract the triage agent fills in. The agent never writes prose directly to an issue: it produces this object, and a separate privileged job renders it into a comment and labels. Validating against this schema at the publish boundary is what makes output-side prompt injection ineffective, so every field is constrained and additionalProperties is false.

schema_version.description: Version of this contract. The publish job rejects anything it does not recognise.

issue_number.description: The issue this triage applies to. The publish job must verify this matches the triggering issue and refuse to post anywhere else.

summary.description: One or two sentences describing the reported problem, in the agent's own words.

issue_kind.description: BUG when the report follows the bug template and describes a defect. Questions and feature requests belong in Discussions and should be redirected.

suggested_area.description: Which component most likely owns the problem. See skills/routing.md for the signature table.

area_confidence.description: HIGH only when a concrete signal was found, such as a stack frame in a named file. Absence of evidence is LOW, never HIGH.

area_evidence.description: The specific signal that drove the routing decision: the failing script and line, or the BcContainerHelper cmdlet in the stack. Required, because a routing decision a maintainer cannot check is worth very little. Write 'No concrete signal found' if there genuinely is none - and then area_confidence must be LOW.

traced_locations.description: Source locations found by actually searching the repository, not guessed. An empty array is allowed only with area_confidence LOW: HIGH confidence or a non-unknown fix_risk without any traced location is rejected at publish, because guessing which file is at fault is the single most misleading thing this agent can do.

line.description: Line number. Required: `git grep -n` gives this for free, and 'somewhere in this file' wastes the reader's time. If you cannot name a line, you have not traced it.

excerpt.description: The actual line or few lines of code, quoted verbatim - not paraphrased. A maintainer should be able to confirm the diagnosis without opening the file.

why.description: What this location has to do with the reported symptom, specifically. 'Handles the artifact logic' is useless; 'throws when no release matches, with no fallback to latest' is useful.

has_missing_information.description: Whether information genuinely needed to investigate is absent. Not simply whether a template field was left blank.

missing_information.description: A concise sentence naming only the important missing items, or 'None'.

linked_run.description: The workflow run the reporter linked, if any. Most reporters' repositories are private, so an unreadable run is the common case and is not the reporter's fault.

troubleshooting_requirement.description: Whether the reporter should run the Troubleshooting workflow. REQUIRED when no usable logs exist and the symptom cannot be traced statically.

algo_version.description: The AL-Go version as stated by the reporter, normalized, or 'Not provided'.

fixed_in_release.description: If the symptom matches a RELEASENOTES.md entry newer than the reporter's version, the release that fixed it. Empty otherwise.

reproduction_quality.description: Whether the reported steps are enough to investigate.

repro_outcome.description: Result of the Tier 1 action-script repro. COULD_NOT_CONSTRUCT is an expected, common and honest outcome - most notably for actions classified 'unsafe' in the repro policy - and must not be presented to the reporter as a dismissal.

repro_manifest.description: The repro manifest that was run, conforming to Tests/Repro/repro-manifest.schema.json. Present only when repro_outcome is REPRODUCED or NOT_REPRODUCED.

duplicate_candidates.description: Up to five possible duplicates, most likely first. Empty when none found.

fix_risk.description: Blast radius of a likely fix, from skills/risk-tiers.md. Use 'unknown' when the affected code could not be identified - never guess 'low'.

fix_risk_reason.description: Why that risk level, naming the files or areas a fix would touch.

recommended_lane.description: What should happen next. 'needs-human-fix' is required whenever fix_risk is critical.

suggested_labels.description: Labels to apply. The publish job intersects this with its own allow-list, so anything unexpected here is silently dropped rather than trusted.

notes_for_maintainer.description: Detail useful to a maintainer but not posted to the issue, such as the traced code path or assumptions made while reconstructing the repro.
